_meta.indication: AZSTARYS is a CNS stimulant indicated for the treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in patients 6 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 (Study KP415.E01 was one of two phase 3 trials in the KP415 development program; single pivotal efficacy study sufficient given prior finding of efficacy of Focalin XR)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, dose-optimized, randomized, placebo-controlled laboratory classroom design, with a ~3-week open-label dose-optimization phase followed by a 1-week double-blind placebo-controlled phase with lab classroom on Day 28
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ages 6 to 12 years with ADHD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Difference between KP415 and placebo in the average of the mean changes from baseline on the SKAMP combined score (SKAMP-C) across all post-dose time points on the classroom day (Day 28)
pivotal_trials.result: KP415 was superior to placebo on the primary SKAMP-C outcome on Day 28, with a LS mean average change from baseline treatment difference of -5.4 (95% CI: -7.1, -3.7); p<0.001 (protocol-specified analysis)

nct_ctgov.title: KP415 Classroom Study in Children (6-12 Years of Age) With ADHD

key_safety: Most common (>5% and twice the rate of placebo) adverse reactions include appetite decreased, insomnia, nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, weight decreased, anxiety, dizziness, irritability, affect lability, tachycardia, and blood pressure increased. Serious risks include serious cardiovascular reactions (sudden death) and long-term suppression of growth.
target_moa: d-MPH is a CNS stimulant that blocks the reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine into the presynaptic neuron and increases their release into the extraneuronal space; SDX is an inactive prodrug converted to d-MPH in the gastrointestinal tract
modality: Small molecule (fixed-combination stimulant: serdexmethylphenidate, a prodrug of dexmethylphenidate, plus immediate-release dexmethylphenidate)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ABUSE AND DEPENDENCE — CNS stimulants, including AZSTARYS, other methylphenidate-containing products, and amphetamines, have a high potential for abuse and dependence; assess the risk of abuse prior to prescribing and monitor for signs of abuse and dependence while on therapy

rems.type: No REMS were deemed to be necessary to ensure the benefits for this product outweigh its risks

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial designs were acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear

basis.text: This was a standard (not priority) review

summary.text: AZSTARYS (KP415) was approved as an NME 505(b)(2) NDA under standard review for the treatment of ADHD in patients 6 years and older; SDX is a new molecular entity that is an inactive prodrug of dexmethylphenidate. No advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.
